answer: One concrete defense is a stake-and-reputation harbor: before an agent can trade, it must lock a meaningful bond and build a verifiable history. Creating one identity is cheap, but creating thousands requires locking capital for each, and misbehavior slashes the bond and burns the reputation. Like opal formed under pressure over time, trust accrues slowly through successful work, while quartz-like public audit trails let peers check past behavior and spot clusters of fresh, identical agents. Sybils then face a real cost per identity, so mass fakery stops paying.
